{"consolidated_memory":"**Loss divergence in ml/train/loop.py: Four distinct incidents**

Component: ml/train/loop.py (ml pipeline), covered by tests/ml/test_train_loop.py
Symptom across all: Loss curve turns upward and never returns
Reproduction: Train two epochs on the small split
Stack: Python

**Occasion 1: [2026-01-21]**
- Trigger: Jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary
- Root cause: Missing Unicode normalization before hashing
- Fix: Normalized to NFC ahead of the digest (PR #5527, branch fix/loss-divergence-1)
- Outcome: Job finished in 59 minutes instead of 8 hours

**Occasion 2: [2026-04-10]**
- Trigger: Deeply nested inputs beyond six levels
- Root cause: Naive datetime compared against an aware datetime
- Fix: Made every boundary timezone aware at the edge (PR #5768, branch fix/loss-divergence-2)
- Outcome: P99 latency fell from 7.0 s to 434 ms

**Occasion 3: [2026-04-28]**
- Trigger: Two requests racing on the same key
- Root cause: Floating point rounding in the money path
- Fix: Moved the arithmetic to integer minor units (PR #6727, branch fix/loss-divergence-3)
- Outcome: Alert stayed quiet for 44 consecutive days

**Occasion 4: [2026-06-05]**
- Trigger: Payloads above roughly two megabytes
- Root cause: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: Raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it (PR #7356, branch fix/loss-divergence-4)
- Outcome: Memory settled at 166 MB instead of climbing past 9 GB"}
